title: Monday Morning Quarterback: College Saturday review
date_line: Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, updated just after midnight. College Saturday review: the full Nov. 7 slate, graded, including the five late games, plus New Mexico at Nevada and TCU at Arizona from Friday night (Nov. 6). Then next college week.

paragraphs: Saturday put 50 college games with lines on the board, and all 50 are final and graded here. It was a night for broken hearts. Texas A&M +7.5 was covering until a fourth-down sack and a 41-yard touchdown run with 79 seconds left. Kansas −3 was covering until UCF scored on the final snap. Western Kentucky +1.5 was covering with one second left and lost by 7.5. Mississippi State −3 and the Over 48.5 both died on one failed two-point throw, and the Over at West Point died at the Army 1. On the other side of the window, Charlotte +11.5 and Temple +7.5 cashed by half a point apiece, a Louisville touchdown nobody needed pushed the Over 60.5 home by half a point, and out in El Paso, UTEP +9.5 spent three fourth-quarter minutes on the wrong side of the number before clawing back.

Every game below is graded against the line printed on the card at kickoff, using ESPN finals and play-by-play, and a push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. Merrimack at Wake Forest had no line on the card and isn't graded. The heartbreakers go first, then the escapes, then Friday's two late finishes, then the rest of the card.
Follow The Money had a side in only four Saturday games and a total in four, and In The Trenches had a side in 22. Letdown Watch made no picks. Games without a pick aren't graded for them.

This edition was updated just after midnight with the five Saturday games that had not finished when it first went up: West Virginia at Texas Tech, Fresno State at Utah State, Hawai'i at UTEP, Texas State at Oregon State and Wyoming at UNLV. Every handicapper's tickets in those five are graded below, and the records include them.

Card line: South Carolina −7.5, total 51.5. The Cover Writer's card had Texas A&M +7.5 and the Over, projecting South Carolina 28, Texas A&M 26. Final: Texas A&M 9, South Carolina 17. South Carolina won by 8, and the teams scored 26 points.

Texas A&M +7.5 was the ticket you'd have framed by the end of the third quarter. The Aggies led 9-7 after three Olano field goals, and even when Olano pushed a 30-yarder wide and Orsan answered with a 49-yard miss of his own, the Aggie backers were sitting pretty. South Carolina finally took a 10-9 lead on Orsan's 43-yard field goal with 8:14 to play. Texas A&M +7.5 was still covering by 6.5, and the Over 51.5 was long gone at 19 points.

Then the Aggies went for it. Reed was sacked for a loss of 14 yards on fourth down with 1:27 left, a turnover on downs at the A&M 41, and on the very next snap Sellers ran 41 yards for a touchdown. South Carolina 17, Texas A&M 9. Eight points. The +7.5 that had been cashing all afternoon was now losing by half a point.

And Texas A&M still nearly got it back. Reed marched them down the field, Edwards fumbled at the 20 and the Aggies fell on it, Horton caught a 14-yarder to the 10 with eight seconds left, and Reed threw two balls into the end zone, the second one with two seconds on the clock. Both hit the turf. Texas A&M +7.5 lost by half a point, on a fourth-down gamble and a 41-yard run, and the Over 51.5 died 25.5 points short of the window.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on Texas A&M +7.5, missed by 0.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 51.5, fell 25.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the side or the total.
Card line: Kansas −3, total 48.5. The Cover Writer's card had Kansas −3 and the Over, projecting Kansas 29, UCF 25. Final: UCF 33, Kansas 32. UCF won by 1, and the teams scored 65 points.

Kansas −3 was a winning ticket with one second left. That's the whole story, but you deserve the details. Kansas came back from 26-7 down, Connington's 34-yard field goal made it 26-24, and Edwards punched in a 2-yard touchdown with 1:06 to play, with a two-point conversion on top. Kansas 32, UCF 26. Kansas −3 was covering by 3, and the Over 48.5 had cashed long before.

UCF got the ball at its own 27 with a minute to go. Barnett hit Hornes for 20, found Hinshaw for 20 more, and then Derry for 19 to the Kansas 15. With four seconds left, an interference flag on Kansas in the end zone gave UCF one more snap, and Barnett hit Piening from 6 yards out with one second left. Stone's kick made it UCF 33, Kansas 32. Kansas −3 went from a 3-point cover to a 4-point loss on the final snap, and the Over 48.5 was just the consolation prize at 65.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 48.5, cleared it by 16.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on Kansas −3, missed by 4 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the total.

Card line: Middle Tennessee −1.5, total 52.5. The Cover Writer's card had Western Kentucky +1.5 and the Over, projecting Middle Tennessee 28, Western Kentucky 27. Final: Western Kentucky 42, Middle Tennessee 51. Middle Tennessee won by 9, and the teams scored 93 points.

Western Kentucky +1.5 had the comeback, the tie and the ticket in hand with 31 seconds left. Down 42-35, Tisdale moved the Hilltoppers to the Middle Tennessee 20, an interference flag put the ball on the doorstep, and Tisdale ran it in from 5 yards out. Campbell's kick tied it at 42. Western Kentucky +1.5 was covering by 1.5, and the Over 52.5 was buried under 84 points.

Middle Tennessee had 31 seconds to work with. Gagliano hit Butler for 12, Lacy for 23 to the Western Kentucky 40, spiked it, and found Clifton for 7 more to the 33 with four seconds left. Bourgeois drilled a 48-yard field goal with one second on the clock. Middle Tennessee 45, Western Kentucky 42, and the +1.5 had just lost by 1.5.

Then, on the final play, Western Kentucky fumbled, and Singleton recovered it in the end zone for a Middle Tennessee touchdown as time ran out. Middle Tennessee 51, Western Kentucky 42. Western Kentucky +1.5 lost by 7.5 after being a winner 30 seconds earlier, and the Over 52.5 cleared by 40.5.
Called it: Next Man Up and In The Trenches on Middle Tennessee −1.5, covered by 7.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 52.5, cleared it by 40.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer and The Formula on Western Kentucky +1.5, missed by 7.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the total.

Card line: Mississippi State −3, total 48.5. The Cover Writer's card had Mississippi State −3 and the Over, projecting Mississippi State 32, Vanderbilt 23. Final: Vanderbilt 25, Mississippi State 23. Vanderbilt won by 2, and the teams scored 48 points.

Mississippi State −3 and the Over 48.5 both died on the same failed two-point try, and that's a special kind of pain. Vanderbilt led 22-14 after Taylor's 34-yard field goal, and when Ferrie's 26-yarder made it 22-17 with 4:56 left, the Bulldogs had a pulse and the total sat at 39. Then Vanderbilt ran the clock down and Taylor hit a 55-yard field goal with 1:46 to go. Vanderbilt 25, Mississippi State 17. The Over needed 6.5 more, and Mississippi State −3 needed a miracle.

Swann went to work. He found Johnson for 16, Bothwell for 12, and then hit Magee for a 30-yard touchdown with 32 seconds left. That made it 25-23 and 48 points, half a point shy of the Over. Swann's two-point throw failed, the onside kick went 10 yards and Vanderbilt fell on it, and that was the game. Mississippi State −3 lost by 5, and the Over 48.5 missed by half a point on a two-point try that would have tied the game and cashed the total in the same breath.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on Mississippi State −3, missed by 5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 48.5, fell 0.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the side or the total.

Card line: Notre Dame −5.5, total 57.5. The Cover Writer's card had Miami +5.5 and the Over, projecting Notre Dame 33, Miami 29. Final: Miami 24, Notre Dame 31. Notre Dame won by 7, and the teams scored 55 points.

Miami +5.5 and the Over 57.5 both needed one more score, and Notre Dame's defense said no twice. Notre Dame led 31-17 after James' 1-yard touchdown, but Mensah kept coming. Barkate caught a 1-yard touchdown with 9:53 left, and it was 31-24. Miami +5.5 was 1.5 points away, and the total sat at 55, 2.5 short of the Over.

Notre Dame had a chance to end both debates. Porath lined up a 53-yard field goal with 5:49 left and missed it. A make would have put the total at 58 and cashed the Over. Instead Miami took over, Mensah hit Lofton for 41 yards to the Notre Dame 22, and then threw three straight incompletions, the last one broken up by Talich on fourth down. Turnover on downs. Notre Dame ran the clock to under a minute, Miami got one last chance from its own 13, and the final snap ended in a fumble. Notre Dame 31, Miami 24. Miami +5.5 lost by 1.5, and the Over 57.5 fell 2.5 short, one field goal from a cash.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on Miami +5.5, missed by 1.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 57.5, fell 2.5 points short.

Card line: Florida International −4, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had Florida International −4 and the Under, projecting Florida International 26, Missouri State 21. Final: Missouri State 20, Florida International 23. Florida International won by 3, and the teams scored 43 points.

Florida International −4 needed a four-point win and got a three-point win on the final snap. The Panthers led 17-6 early in the fourth after Lyons' 17-yard touchdown run. Then Missouri State's Cooper scooped a fumble and went 51 yards for a touchdown, with Belin running in the two-point try to tie it at 17. Czeremcha put Florida International back up 20-17 with a 42-yard field goal at 1:55, and Missouri State answered with Obeid's 30-yarder to tie it again.

Czeremcha got one more try and hit from 35 as time ran out. Florida International 23, Missouri State 20. The home fans went home happy, and the Florida International −4 tickets went in the trash by one point. The Under 50.5 was never in trouble at 43.
Called it: The Formula and In The Trenches on Missouri State +4, covered by 1 point. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Under 50.5, stayed under by 7.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer and Next Man Up on Florida International −4, missed by 1 point.

Card line: Army −3.5, total 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had Army −3.5 and the Over, projecting Army 31, Air Force 25. Final: Air Force 24, Army 21. Air Force won by 3, and the teams scored 45 points.

Army −3.5 and the Over 47.5 went down together at West Point, and Army's own goal-to-go stand is what finished off the Over. Army led 21-17 after Luter's 19-yard touchdown run late in the third, and Army −3.5 was covering by half a point. Then Medders hit Kibbee for a 24-yard touchdown on the first play of the fourth. Air Force 24, Army 21, 45 points on the board, and the Over needed just one more field goal.

Army's next drive died when Hellums was intercepted by Johnson at the Air Force 44. Air Force then marched to the Army 1 and got stuffed on fourth down at the Army 1 with 7:11 left. A touchdown there cashes the Over by 4.5, and Army's goal-to-go stand kept the total at 45. Army got the ball at its own 1, went three-and-out, punted, and Air Force knelt it out from the Army 20. Army −3.5 lost by 6.5, and the Over 47.5 died 2.5 points short.
Called it: The Formula on Air Force +3.5, covered by 6.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on Army −3.5, missed by 6.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 47.5, fell 2.5 points short.

Card line: Utah −4, total 49.5. The Cover Writer's card had Utah −4 and the Over, projecting Utah 30, BYU 22. Final: BYU 20, Utah 28. Utah won by 8, and the teams scored 48 points.

The Over 49.5 in Salt Lake City died twice in the end zone. Utah led 28-20 after Dampier's 3-yard touchdown run with 12:03 to play, and the total sat at 48, 1.5 points from home. BYU just needed a touchdown from somewhere. Bachmeier drove the Cougars deep into Utah territory, and Reynolds intercepted him at the goal with 4:39 left. BYU got one last chance, and with 13 seconds left Bachmeier was intercepted in the end zone again, this time by Ritchie.

Utah 28, BYU 20. The Over 49.5 fell 1.5 points short, done in by two end-zone interceptions. The flip side is the escape: Utah −4 covered by exactly 4 points, and the BYU touchdown that would have cashed the Over would have killed the Utah ticket. One stadium, two very different nights.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on Utah −4, covered by 4 points.

Card line: UAB −11.5, total 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had Charlotte +11.5 and the Over, projecting UAB 33, Charlotte 22. Final: Charlotte 12, UAB 23. UAB won by 11, and the teams scored 35 points.

Charlotte +11.5 was dead and buried with two minutes left, and then it wasn't. UAB led 23-6 after Simpkins' second short touchdown with 2:07 to go. That's a 17-point margin, and Charlotte +11.5 was losing by 5.5. The Over 47.5 was long gone at 29.

Harrell took the 49ers down the field and hit Barnes for a 14-yard touchdown with 1:01 left. The two-point throw failed, and it didn't matter. UAB 23, Charlotte 12. An 11-point loss, and Charlotte +11.5 cashed by half a point on a backdoor touchdown that nobody in Birmingham will remember and every Charlotte backer will never forget.

Card line: Navy −7.5, total 53.5. The Cover Writer's card had Temple +7.5 and the Under, projecting Navy 30, Temple 23. Final: Temple 35, Navy 42. Navy won by 7, and the teams scored 77 points.

Temple +7.5 looked like the worst ticket in Annapolis at halftime. Gutierrez scored four rushing touchdowns, the last a 6-yarder with 1:14 left in the half, and Navy led 28-0. Bermudez took a punt back 78 yards to make it 28-7 at the break, and that was the first sign of life.

Then Temple came all the way back. Freeman caught a 6-yard touchdown, Navy's Gutierrez fumbled at midfield, Brown punched one in from a yard out, and Smolik hit Freeman from 25 yards out with 5:35 left. Temple 35, Navy 35. Temple +7.5 was covering by 7.5.

Navy had one more answer. Gutierrez ran it in from 4 yards out with 1:14 left for his fifth rushing touchdown of the day. Navy 42, Temple 35. A seven-point loss, and Temple +7.5 cashed by half a point after trailing by 28. The Under 53.5 was already dead and buried at 77.
Called it: The Cover Writer and The Formula on Temple +7.5, covered by 0.5 points. The Formula on the Over 53.5, cleared it by 23.5 points.
Missed: Next Man Up on Navy −7.5, missed by 0.5 points. The Cover Writer and Next Man Up on the Under 53.5, went over by 23.5 points.

Card line: Louisville −14.5, total 60.5. The Cover Writer's card had Georgia Tech +14.5 and the Over, projecting Louisville 38, Georgia Tech 25. Final: Louisville 44, Georgia Tech 17. Louisville won by 27, and the teams scored 61 points.

The Over 60.5 in Atlanta needed a late touchdown from somebody, and Louisville delivered it. The Cardinals led 37-10 after Brown's 11-yard touchdown run in the third, and the total sat at 47. Adamson hit Corbo for an 11-yard touchdown with 4:15 left, and the total climbed to 54, still 6.5 short.

Louisville could have knelt on it. Instead Jennings went in from 2 yards out with 1:56 left, Hilbert's kick made it 44-17, and the total landed at 61. The Over 60.5 cashed by half a point on a touchdown the Cardinals didn't need. Georgia Tech +14.5 lost by 12.5, and Adamson's interception on the next snap sealed it.

San José State −10 survived a late Northern Illinois touchdown by one point. The Spartans led 30-13 after Rolovich hit McKenzie for a 29-yard touchdown in the third. San José State −10 was covering by 7, and the Under 52.5 sat at 43.

Dickens ran it in from a yard out with 3:55 left, and Northern Illinois went for two to cut it to 9. The try failed. San José State 30, Northern Illinois 19. An 11-point win, and San José State −10 covered by one point. The Under 52.5 got home with 3.5 to spare, and Sinatra's missed 46-yarder before the half looks a lot less important now.

Card line: Baylor −9.5, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had Baylor −9.5 and the Over, projecting Baylor 31, Iowa State 21. Final: Iowa State 31, Baylor 42. Baylor won by 11, and the teams scored 73 points.

Baylor −9.5 was a 19-point cushion with four minutes left and ended up a 1.5-point escape. Morris ran 11 yards for a touchdown with 4:11 to go, Baylor led 42-23, and the Over 50.5 had cashed long ago at 65. Then Iowa State came back for one more. Raynor ran it in from 3 yards out with 1:45 left and added the two-point conversion. Baylor 42, Iowa State 31. An 11-point win, and Baylor −9.5 covered by 1.5. The Over 50.5 cleared by 22.5.

Card line: Florida State −5.5, total 53.5. The Cover Writer's card had Florida State −5.5 and the Over, projecting Florida State 31, Boston College 23. Final: Florida State 31, Boston College 24. Florida State won by 7, and the teams scored 55 points.

Florida State −5.5 and the Over 53.5 both landed with 1.5 points to spare, and both came on the same run. The game was tied 24-24 after Panikowski's 22-yard field goal early in the fourth. Florida State −5.5 was losing by 5.5, and the total sat at 48, 5.5 short.

Thomas broke an 11-yard touchdown run with 2:29 left, and Panikowski's kick made it Florida State 31, Boston College 24. That one drive covered Florida State −5.5 by 1.5 and cleared the Over 53.5 by 1.5, and Boston College's last drive went nowhere. A three-interception mess earlier in the game kept everybody nervous.

Card line: Liberty −17.5, total 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had New Mexico State +17.5 and the Under, projecting Liberty 31, New Mexico State 16. Final: Liberty 30, New Mexico State 14. Liberty won by 16, and the teams scored 44 points.

New Mexico State +17.5 held on by a point and a half. Liberty led 23-14 after Davis ran 8 yards for a touchdown with 10:12 left, and New Mexico State +17.5 was comfortable. Then Jones scored from a yard out with 1:03 left to make it 30-14, and New Mexico State +17.5 was hanging on by 1.5. Hedden was intercepted with 16 seconds left, and that was it. Liberty 30, New Mexico State 14. New Mexico State +17.5 cashed by 1.5, and the Under 47.5 got home by 3.5.

Card line: Auburn −10.5, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had Arkansas +10.5 and the Under, projecting Auburn 29, Arkansas 19. Final: Arkansas 23, Auburn 26. Auburn won by 3, and the teams scored 49 points.

Arkansas +10.5 was never in danger, but the Under 50.5 had to survive the last two minutes. Auburn led 23-16 after Brown found Singleton for a 28-yard touchdown with 3:56 left, and Jackson answered with a 23-yard strike to Jordan with 1:54 left. Tied at 23. The total sat at 46, 4.5 short of the Over 50.5, and a touchdown either way would have killed the Under.

Auburn got a field goal instead. McPherson's 43-yarder with 33 seconds left made it Auburn 26, Arkansas 23, and the total landed at 49. Arkansas tried a lateral-fest on the final play and fumbled. Arkansas +10.5 covered by 7.5, and the Under 50.5 stayed under by 1.5, three points from a heartbreak.

Kennesaw State +2.5 was a winner outright, but it took a failed two-point try to make sure. Kinney's 35-yard field goal put the Owls up 42-34 with 8:25 left, and the Under 55.5 had died hours earlier. Delaware answered, and Minicucci hit Graves for a 17-yard touchdown with 24 seconds left. The two-point throw to tie it failed, and the onside kick went 9 yards. Kennesaw State 42, Delaware 40. Kennesaw State +2.5 covered by 4.5, and the Under 55.5 was buried at 82.

Card line: Hawai'i −9.5, total 48.5. The Cover Writer's card had UTEP +9.5 and the Over, projecting Hawai'i 29, UTEP 20. Final: Hawai'i 17, UTEP 14. Hawai'i won by 3, and the teams scored 31 points.

UTEP +9.5 spent three minutes of the fourth quarter losing by half a point, and then it got the half point back with change. Hawai'i drove to the UTEP 1, got shoved back to the 6 by an illegal substitution flag, and Mikaele ran it in anyway for a 17-7 lead with 10:08 left. Ten points against a 9.5-point number, and every UTEP ticket in the country was underwater.

UTEP answered on the very next drive. Moore III hit Ezinwa for a 15-yard touchdown with 6:57 left, and the Miners were back inside the number. Hawai'i got the ball back, ground its way to the UTEP 21 with two minutes to go, and knelt it out from there. A field goal would only have made it a six-point game, so the kneel-downs cost nobody a ticket, but UTEP backers watched all three of them like they were fourth-and-goal. The end of the first half mattered too: Smith picked off Alejado in the end zone with four seconds left, and it stayed 10-7 at the break. Hawai'i 17, UTEP 14. UTEP +9.5 covered by 6.5, and the Over 48.5 fell 17.5 points short.

Nevada +10.5 and the Over 38.5 were in trouble from the first quarter. Humphrey scored from 2 yards out, Sibley ran 31 yards for a touchdown, and New Mexico led 14-3 at the half after Fernandez's 32-yard field goal. Humphrey's second touchdown and Fa'avae's 25-yard throw to Keith made it 28-3, and Romero's 37-yard field goal capped it. New Mexico 31, Nevada 3. Nevada +10.5 lost by 17.5, and the Over 38.5 fell 4.5 points short with Nevada scoring a single field goal.

Arizona −6.5 won the game and lost the ticket. TCU led 28-20 after Jaden Craig ran in from 2 yards out with 6:35 left, and that touchdown also killed the Under 46.5 at 48. Arizona came back. hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: The Cover Writer went 25-25 against the spread and 23-27 on totals Saturday, and the week stands at 30-32 on sides and 28-34 on totals. The late games were kind: West Virginia, Utah State, UTEP and Texas State all covered, and only Wyoming's upset of UNLV kept it from a sweep on sides. Friday finished 2-3 on both after Nevada and Arizona came up short in the late games. Saturday had real heartbreak in it: Texas A&M by half a point, Kansas on the last snap, Western Kentucky with a second left, and the Over in the Vanderbilt game by half a point on a failed two-point try. It also had the escapes, Charlotte and Temple by half a point each, Florida State by a point and a half on both the side and the total, and UTEP hanging on in El Paso. Close calls make good stories, but the grade is the grade, and the grade says even on Saturday and under water for the week.

The Formula went 31-19 against the spread and 21-29 on totals Saturday, 35-27 and 24-38 for the week. The Formula went against the Cover Writer on 14 Saturday sides and won 10 of them, including Tulsa +1.5 by 51.5 points, Iowa +2.5, Air Force +3.5 and Missouri State +4 by a single point. The late games took two of those back, Fresno State −2.5 and Hawai'i −9.5, and then it went 21-29 on totals, so the victory lap can stay short.

Next Man Up went 19-31 against the spread and 23-27 on totals Saturday, 26-36 and 29-33 for the week. Next Man Up walked into Saturday with the best record on the desk and walked out with the worst Saturday on sides of anybody with a full card, and laying 17.5 with Texas Tech at midnight did not help. The lead on sides is gone, though it still holds a one-game lead on the Cover Writer in totals and will mention it every chance it gets.

Follow The Money went 0-4 against the spread and 2-2 on totals Saturday, 3-5 and 6-5 for the week. The money cashed TCU +6.5 and the Over in Tucson on Friday night, then took BYU, Syracuse, Boston College and Minnesota on Saturday and lost all four. The money found the window Friday and lost the map Saturday.

In The Trenches went 12-10 against the spread and made no total picks Saturday, 16-11 for the week. The perfect week died Friday night in Tucson with Arizona −6.5, and Fresno State −2.5 got pushed around in Logan late Saturday, but it was a winning day anyway: Michigan State +12.5 and Oregon +7 won outright, and Missouri State +4 and Middle Tennessee −1.5 cashed on the final plays of their games.
Letdown Watch made no picks Saturday, and it hasn't made one all week.
